title: Rust aim down sights puts the sight's notch on the camera axis
note: A demo named ads holds aim and returns the sight's notch projected to the screen, within 3% of the centre.
intent: Aiming that does not put the sight where the shot goes is worse than none. The viewmodel is drawn in camera space, so ADS is exact arithmetic, not tuning by eye: keep the sight's notch as a const in the gun's space, and the ADS pose is the camera-space offset that puts that notch on the axis (x and y the negation of the notch's, at a chosen depth). Ease a world value aim from 0 to 1 over about 150 ms in on_update and lerp the gun between the hip and the ADS offset by it. Register game.demo("ads", ..) that holds aim, advances a few hundred ms and returns { sightNdc: {x, y}, crosshairVisible } so the board can measure it.

check.name: ads
check.note: A demo named ads holds aim and returns { sightNdc: {x, y} } — the sight's notch over its depth in camera space; within 3% of the screen's centre.

port: The viewmodel facet owns the sight constant, the hip and ADS offsets and the ads demo; the player facet sets the aim intent from input.

evidence.note: game.demo with DemoDriver::sim_mut and advance_ms; a demo's returned Value is what a check reads.
